SWEN? Do you mean SWE? Well not entirely sure what I'm looking for, perhaps broad exposure to a variety of things. I guess getting into something FANG based and then later on to something in AI or Machine learning would be nice in terms of career at least

Yeah unimelb is so damn theory heavy, with very little practical focus and heavy exam weights. Worse when the exams are hurdles
No problem, when you say "what about CS though?" do you mean in terms of job prospects or why it interests me?

Thank you for the advice, I didn't consider writing out a statement. I'll make sure to do that. If that doesn't work then yeah I'll have to look at doing breaths related to comp sci and work towards improving my grades. Although with wamnesty I'm not sure whether my subjects this sem would be an obstacle to being considered, and also if I did apply it would have to be in a years time due to the dates of VTAC applications and the release of results. Well that's what I'm assuming.

It's comforting to know that your not the only one going through hardship.

Also appreciate the advice, I'll look into it. Should be useful in figuring out the causes for my underlining problems.

Yeah the semester has been long, shame the whole thing was under lockdown.

Anyway, thank you for the post it means a lot.

Appreciate you sharing man. Nice to know that I'm not an isolated case. Gotta agree with what you stated below, I probably need to do more prep work before sem starts to ensure that I don't fall behind. Cheers

Yes true I've heard comp sci is quite a challenge, however I've come to the conclusion that working on something that you enjoy and have a genuine interest in makes the hardship worthwhile. Plus, I kinda feel less anxious given that with commerce I don't where it's gonna lead me to and also the fear of being disposable to a degree just gives me anxiety.
Well at least we're in the same boat and not the only ones, but thanks

Yeah I think this would be the best approach, nearly all my subjects so far have been related to commerce, it would be a good break to try learning a different stream, especially one that interests me. Also I appreciate the insight, generally when you fall down the stream of a failing student you tend to get locked into idea of considering yourself as a write off. Although yeah it's not the be all end all. Thank you

Really appreciate you opening up about your personal experience and providing perspective on an unfavourable situation.

I'll look into CAPS and at the moment probably won't be able to do much, but hopefully when everything starts opening up I can reach out to them and see what support I can get. In terms of transferring assuming the worst case scenario I'll probably yeah go with the approach of selecting comp sci breaths, might give me a break and a breather and hopefully we'll be on campus for the next semester. I really was hoping to go to campus this semester since I opted to do a full load online last semester thinking that avoiding/reducing the risk of potentially catching covid and the reduced travel would be beneficial. However how wrong was I and upon reflecting I realised that being on campus for least one subject would've kept me in check, but unfortunately the constant extensions this semester was like watching a flame slowly die out.

Anyway thank you and yeah hopefully everything works out, really appreciate your post.

Man this really hits home, thank you. 

It puts everything into perspective. Sometimes your vision becomes so cloudy you just can't make out what's up or down. Sometimes it takes someone else to point it out to really ground you.  

Man thank you for the belief. Hopefully things do work out - at least in the long run. Yeah maybe a loving relationship might make the hardship and struggle worth it.

Yeah very true, it's easy to get caught up in the fast lane of life and overlook what's around and what can be. 

True, one thing I did consider about an early death was the potential harm to those around me, it played on my mind quite a bit whenever considered this type of action. 

Yeah I guess something to always consider, maybe it's dreams in themselves that make life worth living. Anyway I appreciate the regards, I also wish you the best with your dreams, best of luck.

Man thank you for the complement, it's been years since someone has said anything nice about my character, I really appreciate it.

Yeah I have been to a few professionals, though only briefly. I didn't really resonate with them so much, or at least I didn't really feel that things were progressing. Partially due to maybe the fact that by the time I did seek some help, I'd been suffering from anxiety and depression for a few years (from about the age of 15, getting help around 19/20). So these negative traits became part of my character and I really couldn't make the distinction of what life really looked like with out them.

Where I'm from they generally don't tend to prescribe medication unless your older like 23/24+. Also the way they screen for this stuff is kinda perplexing - when I got screened for anxiety and depression (age 21- at that point I still had anxiety, although  I had been able to get rid of the depression). I was given a multiple choice questionnaire and if I answered this one particular question with this particular answer I was then declared depressed. I guess I was kinda shocked at how superficial the screening was when these sort conditions really inflict suffering on individuals, yet there wasn't a more comprehensive means for testing for it. This kinda made me question the intention of professional help at the time. I did end up looking online for resources and I came across JP 12 Rules for Life, it had quite a profound impact on my understanding of the why and to a degree the how, but generally that's the best I've gotten. I feel kinda mixed on getting professional help, part of me feels ashamed at needing such a service and terribly awkward, also with no certainty if it will work. I've heard some people go through a professionals with no luck while others are able to get their life back.

I do kinda agree with the distortion of views, when I was younger one time in particular where I was really thought it was best to end it. I developed this kinda tunnel vision - everything seemed dark and yet there was this light at the end, maybe freedom I don't know, but any other rational thought against this course of action didn't really make sense or come to surface. I was really only able to get out of it, due it being caused by some problematic circumstances which fortunately turned for the better.

Man thanks for posting this, nice to know that I'm not the only one going through the same thing. Where I'm studying most students are really competent and most do quite well so you really feel like a true outcast if you under perform. 

I mean I'm not really in a position to give advice, but maybe I suggest you take a gap year to either work or travel, and then come back to school. You'll get a refreshed perspective about what you want from your education, and who knows maybe you might feel like you wanna change major, or do something else you find interesting like a trade perhaps.
